title: Locality Reservation Admission Controller: capacity-aware geo pinning with circuit-breaker integration
creator: Ava Patel
description: Implement an admission controller that performs locality reservation and capacity-aware geo pinning for incoming inference requests. The controller will use per-region credit reservoirs, latency tiers, and an integrated circuit-breaker evaluator to decide: allow to preferred region, fallback to a nearby region, or shed/queue request. Goal: keep P95 generation latency within SLOs during regional load spikes while preserving cache locality and bounding cross-region cost.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller accepts requests to preferred region when region credits > reservation_threshold and recent latency quantiles are healthy
When preferred region capacity is constrained, controller falls back to configured tiered list (same hemisphere -> adjacent -> global) and records fallback metric
Circuit-breaker trips and causes immediate conservative shedding for region when error rate or tail latency breach window-spec exceeds configured thresholds
End-to-end SLO dashboard shows P95 latency degradation < 20% vs baseline during controlled overload tests and failover drills
E2E tests cover hedged/fallback flows, cache-warm/cold scenarios, and admission rejections with clear metrics and annotated traces
Rollout can be toggled per-customer and per-model via feature flags in console with safe rollback
Documentation and runbook published with explicit operator steps for a regional evacuation and recovery
implementation_steps: Design: finalize credit reservoir model (sliding-window credits + decay) and define reservation_threshold, min_credit_reserve
Design: define latency tiers and fallback topology per region; wire to existing region metadata service
Prototype: admission controller service that reads region health snapshots and credit state from Redis and exposes a deterministic decision API
Integrate: hook controller into request director path with non-blocking fast-fail path and metrics emission
Circuit-breaker: implement multi-signal evaluator (error-rate, 99.9th latency, token depletion) with exponential backoff open window
Testing: create chaos tests to simulate regional CPU/GPU saturation, network egress spikes, and KV cache thrash
Observability: emit decision_reason tag, chosen_region, fallback_hop_count, credit_before_after, and circuit_state into tracing and metrics
Rollout: gradual canary on low-traffic customers, ramp to 50% per-region, then global; monitor SLO and cost metrics
technical_notes: We are avoiding hard pinning to preserve cache locality while allowing graceful degradation. Credit reservoir uses a 60s sliding window with per-region burst allowance. Trade-offs: aggressive pinning reduces cross-region cost but can cause long tails if regional capacity hits GPU saturation. Conservative design biases towards preserving SLOs at cost of increased inter-region traffic. Circuit-breaker is tuned to prefer shedding user requests early (503) rather than returning high-latency responses that violate SLOs and downstream cascades.
decisions: Use Redis for short-lived credit state to enable fast reads/writes across director instances
Fallback topology will be hemisphere-aware before global to minimize cross-continent egress cost
Admission controller will emit detailed decision_reason tags for post-mortem analysis
Circuit-breaker open state requires both error-rate AND P99 latency breach to prevent noisy opens during transient load spikes
tradeoffs: Keeping larger per-region credits reduces fallbacks but increases risk of overload and cache misses; we limit credit size to 2x median throughput
Preferring latency-optimal region increases cost (egress, cross-region model state sync) but preserves user experience
Shed early vs queue: shedding returns explicit failures to clients which is easier to observe; queuing adds complexity and tail-latency risk

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Busy-wait or synchronous calls in director path could add latency. Mitigation: decision API is in-process library with async background sync to Redis when possible.
Risk: Redis single-region outage could impair global decisioning. Mitigation: replicate minimal credit state to a read-only region and fallback to latency-tier routing when control plane unavailable.
Risk: Overly aggressive circuit-breaker could cause customer-visible failures. Mitigation: introduce warmup periods, gradual thresholds, and automatic rollback triggers tied to SLOs.
